Summary: This bill would establish a task force to study options for making street design and infrastructure safer for pedestrians, motorists, cyclists, and operators of electric bicycles and electric scooters, in consideration of the increased use of, and collisions involving, electric bicycles and electric scooters in New York City. The task force would submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the Council with recommendations for legislation and policy within 480 days of the law taking effect.
Text:
A Local Law in relation to the establishment of a task force to study options for legislation and policy relating to making street design and infrastructure safer in consideration of the increased use of, and number of collisions involving, electric bicycles and electric scooters

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Definitions. For purposes of this local law, the following terms have the following meanings:
City. The term “city” means the city of New York.
Electric bicycle. The term “electric bicycle” has the same meaning as the term “bicycle with electric assist” as set forth in section 102-c of the vehicle and traffic law. 
Electric scooter. The term “electric scooter” has the same meaning as set forth in section 114-e of the vehicle and traffic law.
Task force. The term “task force” means the task force established by this local law.
§ 2. Task force established. There is hereby established a task force to be known as the micromobility street safety task force.
§ 3. Duties. The task force shall study options for legislation and policy relating to street design and infrastructure to make streets safer for pedestrians, motorists, cyclists, and operators of electric bicycles and electric scooters, in consideration of the increased use of electric bicycles and electric scooters and the increased number of collisions involving an electric bicycle or electric scooter in the city. The task force shall make recommendations for legislation and policy in furtherance of such objective. The task force shall consider:
a. Existing laws, rules, and policies related to the use of, or collisions involving, electric bicycles or electric scooters in the city; any initiatives to provide public education and awareness about such laws, rules, and policies; and the enforcement of such laws and rules;
b. The street design and infrastructure of locations where collisions involving an electric bicycle or electric scooter frequently occur, as determined by the task force;
c. Any legislation and policy implemented in municipalities other than the city to address any increased use of electric bicycles or electric scooters, or any increase in the number of collisions involving an electric bicycle or electric scooter, in such municipalities;
d. Any anticipated effects of the recommendations of the task force on pedestrians, motorists, cyclists, operators of electric bicycles and electric scooters, including persons who use an electric bicycle or electric scooter as a primary mode of transportation for any commercial purpose, and persons with disabilities; 
e. Any data available on the increased use of electric bicycles or electric scooters, or the increased number of collisions involving an electric bicycle or electric scooter, in the city, disaggregated, to the extent feasible, by borough and council district; 
f. Any gaps in the collection of such data, or in the public disclosure of any such data required to be made public;
g. The projected costs to the city and other stakeholders of implementing any recommendations of the task force; and
h. Any other considerations the task force deems relevant.
§ 4. Membership. a. The task force shall be composed of the following members:
1. The deputy mayor who oversees the department of transportation, or such deputy mayor’s designee, who shall serve as chair;
2. The commissioner of transportation, or such commissioner’s designee; 
3. Two members appointed by the mayor who are not employed by any agency; and
4. Three members appointed by the speaker of the council, one of whom shall be a representative of a delivery worker advocacy organization, one of whom shall be a representative of a disability rights advocacy organization, and one of whom shall be a representative of a street safety advocacy organization or an organization that advocates for victims of collisions involving an electric bicycle or electric scooter.
b. All appointments required by this section shall be made no later than 90 days after the effective date of this local law.
c. Each appointed member of the task force shall serve at the pleasure of the officer who appointed such member. In the event of a vacancy on the task force, a successor shall be appointed in the same manner as the original appointment. All members of the task force shall serve without compensation.
§ 5. Meetings. a. The chair shall convene the first meeting of the task force no later than 30 days after the appointment of all members of the task force, except that where not all members of the task force have been appointed within the time specified in subdivision b of section four of this local law, the chair shall convene the first meeting of the task force within 10 days of the appointment of a sufficient number of members to constitute a quorum.
b. The chair shall invite experts and stakeholders to attend meetings of the task force and to provide information relevant to the duties of the task force. 
c. The chair may invite officers and representatives of any relevant federal, state, or local agency or public authority to participate in the work of the task force.
d. The task force shall meet no less than once each quarter until the task force submits the report required by section six of this local law. 
e. The task force shall hold at least 5 town hall meetings, which may be conducted virtually, with each borough receiving at least 1 town hall meeting directed primarily to the residents of such borough, to receive input from members of the public, prior to submitting the report required by section six of this local law. The task force shall conduct outreach to inform the public of each such town hall meeting, and in addition, further direct such outreach to transit deserts and other areas that are insufficiently serviced by mass transportation options. 
§ 6. Report. a. No later than 480 days after the effective date of this local law, the task force shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report setting forth recommendations for legislation and policy relating to street design and infrastructure to make streets safer for pedestrians, motorists, cyclists, and operators of electric bicycles and electric scooters. The report shall include a summary of the information the task force considered in formulating its recommendations. The report may include a recommendation supported by less than a majority of members of the task force, provided that the report shall note the number of members who supported inclusion of any such recommendation.
b. The task force shall post the report on the website of the city no later than 10 days after the date on which the task force submits the report to the mayor and the speaker of the council.
§ 7. Agency support. Any agency designated by the mayor shall provide staff and resources to support the work of the task force.
§ 8. Termination. The task force shall terminate on the date on which the task force submits the report required by section six of this local law.
§ 9. This local law takes effect immediately.
